## Function Snapshot Targets

Remembers the bytes (or absence) of every target before writing.

Behaviour: snapshotTargets(root, targets) reads each target under root, in targets order: a regular file gives its bytes (any bytes, never decoded), anything else gives null (absent). In memory, never through git. restoreSnapshot puts every entry back: bytes are written again (parent directories created), null deletes the file if it exists. Restoring twice is the same as restoring once.

Steps:
- produces: Target Snapshot

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given root with src/a.ts = "old\n" and no src/b.ts; snapshot of targets [src/a.ts, src/b.ts]; then src/a.ts written "new\n" and src/b.ts written "x\n"; when the snapshot is restored; then entries are [src/a.ts with 4 bytes "old\n", src/b.ts with bytes null]; after restore src/a.ts reads "old\n" and src/b.ts does not exist
2. given root with src/deep/a.ts = "old\n"; snapshot of [src/deep/a.ts]; then the directory src/deep removed; when the snapshot is restored, then restored again; then src/deep/a.ts reads "old\n" after each restore (the parent directory is recreated)
3. given root with bin.dat holding the 4 bytes ff 00 fe 0a (not UTF-8); snapshot of [bin.dat]; then bin.dat written "text\n"; when the snapshot is restored; then bin.dat holds exactly the bytes ff 00 fe 0a (hex "ff00fe0a")

Data Target Snapshot: The bytes of a card's targets before any variant is written.
Schema:
{ root: string, entries: { path: string, bytes: Uint8Array | null }[] } — entries in targets order, null = absent

## Function Run Acceptance

Executes the card's acceptance command from the repo root.

Behaviour: runAcceptance(command, root, {env, timeoutMs}) spawns /bin/sh -c with cwd = root, env = the given env with NO_COLOR=1 and CI=1 laid over it (nothing else; the caller passes what it wants inherited), detached in its own process group; stdout and stderr merged in write order. timeoutMs defaults to 300000: on expiry the whole process group is killed, so no child outlives the call, and the result is exit null, timedOut true, the output so far kept with the line "acceptance timed out after <ms> ms" appended. The log is clipped by clipLog: over 4000 chars it keeps the first 1500 and the last 1500 chars and, between them, a marker and every middle line that looks like a diagnosis (FAIL, Error, assert, expected), within 800 chars. Returns Acceptance Result.

Steps:
- produces: Acceptance Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given command `echo out; echo err >&2; exit 3`, env {PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin"}; when run; then {exit: 3, log: "out\nerr\n", timedOut: false}

Data Acceptance Result: What one acceptance command run returned.
Schema:
{ exit: number | null, log: string, timedOut: boolean }

## Function Verify Card

Best-of-N over the parsed variants.

Behaviour: verifyCard({root, targets, command, variants, env, timeoutMs}) snapshots the targets once, then for each variant in order: a corrupt answer gives the stand-in result {exit null, log "answer corrupt: <reason>", diff null} and a truncated one {exit null, log "answer truncated", diff null}, nothing written; otherwise every file of the answer is written under root and the acceptance is run; exit 0 → that variant is accepted, its files stay, its result has diff null and no later variant is tried; any other exit → the result carries the Build Attempt Diff of the written files against the snapshot, the snapshot is restored, and the next variant is tried. Returns Verify Outcome; with no green variant accepted is null and the tree equals the snapshot.

Steps:
- reads: Parsed Answer
- calls: Snapshot Targets
- calls: Run Acceptance
- calls: Build Attempt Diff
- produces: Verify Outcome

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given root with src/a.ts = "old\n"; targets [src/a.ts]; command `grep good src/a.ts || { echo "FAIL: no good in src/a.ts"; exit 1; }`; variants c.v1 {corrupt: "missing section for src/a.ts"}, c.v2 {files: {src/a.ts: "bad\n"}}, c.v3 {files: {src/a.ts: "good\n"}}; when verified; then accepted {variant: "c.v3"}; results [{c.v1, exit null, log "answer corrupt: missing section for src/a.ts", diff null}, {c.v2, exit 1, log "FAIL: no good in src/a.ts\n", diff "--- a/src/a.ts\n+++ b/src/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-old\n+bad\n"}, {c.v3, exit 0, log "good\n", diff null}]; src/a.ts reads "good\n"
2. given the same root and command; targets [src/a.ts, src/b.ts], src/b.ts absent; variants c.v1 {truncated: true}, c.v2 {files: {src/a.ts: "bad\n", src/b.ts: "x\n"}}; when verified; then accepted null; results [{c.v1, exit null, log "answer truncated", diff null}, {c.v2, exit 1, log "FAIL: no good in src/a.ts\n", diff "--- a/src/a.ts\n+++ b/src/a.ts\n@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n-old\n+bad\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/src/b.ts\n@@ -0,0 +1,1 @@\n+x\n"}]; src/a.ts reads "old\n" and src/b.ts does not exist
3. given the same root, command and targets [src/a.ts]; variants c.v1 {files: {src/a.ts: "good\n"}}, c.v2 {files: {src/a.ts: "good\n"}}; when verified; then accepted {variant: "c.v1"}; results has exactly one entry, c.v1 with exit 0: c.v2 is never run

Schema:
{ accepted: { variant: string } | null, results: { variant: string, exit: number | null, log: string, diff: string | null }[] }
